subject: economics
title: Poverty Traps and Strategy
welcome_lead: Some countries are stuck - and breaking out needs more than aid.
meta_desc: A-Level Development: poverty traps and development strategies.
final_note: Targeted investment in health, education and infrastructure can unlock growth.

walkthroughs.body_html: Low incomes mean low saving, so low investment, so low productivity and low incomes - a loop. Health and infectious-disease traps work similarly: sickness keeps families poor.
Aid critics argue it props up bad governments and crowds out private effort. Defenders point to vaccine, HIV and infrastructure wins. Effective aid is targeted, measured and conditional.
Modern development strategy blends trade access, infrastructure, education investment, microfinance and selective FDI. No single tool solves poverty; combinations work.

mcqs.q: What does dependency theory argue about development?
options: Dependency theory is about households relying on benefits.
Dependency theory means poor countries are simply lazy.

Poorer 'periphery' countries are kept underdeveloped by their economic relationships with rich 'core' countries — through unequal trade, debt and historical colonialism. It challenges the view that integration with rich economies automatically helps.
Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
